You are a professional code understanding evaluation expert. Please objectively and fairly score the model's answer based on the following information.

## Question Information
**Question Description**: how to edit active window widget

hello everyone
anyhow know how to change active window widget to show only the name of the app open ?
for example i wanna show only "google chrome" and not the name of the tabs open

For example, in my current setup with Visual Studio Code open, the widget shows the full window title including the file name and project details, but I only want it to display "Visual Studio Code".

## Real Repository Information
**Directory Structure**:
```

```

## Model Answer to be Scored
**Model**: GAPA
**Answer**: You can configure the **Active Window widget** to only show the **application name** instead of the full window title by changing its `label` option.

From the documentation for the Active Window widget:

- The default label is:

  ```text
  "{win[title]}"
  ```
  
  This is why you currently see the full window title (tab name, file name, etc.).  
  [docs/widgets/(Widget)-Active-Windows-Title.md, lines 1–7]

You want to use the **process name** (or a friendly app name mapping) instead.

---

## 1. Basic: show the process name only

Change your active window widget configuration so that:

```yaml
active_window:
  type: "yasb.active_window.ActiveWindowWidget"   # name/type may differ in your config
  options:
    label: "{win[process][name]}"
    # keep the rest of your options as they are
```

Explanation (from the default `label_alt` string):  
`label_alt` uses this format:

```text
"[class_name='{win[class_name]}' exe='{win[process][name]}' hwnd={win[hwnd]}]"
```

This shows that `win[process][name]` is available and contains the executable name (e.g. `chrome.exe`, `Code.exe`).  
[docs/widgets/(Widget)-Active-Windows-Title.md, lines 3–5]

So using `label: "{win[process][name]}"` will display only that.

---

## 2. Optional: map process names to friendly names

If you don’t want `chrome.exe` or `Code.exe` and instead want **"Google Chrome"**, **"Visual Studio Code"**, etc., you can use the `rewrite` option, which is specifically provided “for the widget”:

```text
| `rewrite`           | dict | [See below](#rewrite-options) | Rewrite options for the widget. |
[docs/widgets/(Widget)-Active-Windows-Title.md, lines 16–17]
```

A typical pattern (conceptual example) is:

```yaml
active_window:
  type: "yasb.active_window.ActiveWindowWidget"
  options:
    label: "{win[process][name]}"
    rewrite:
      processes:
        - match: "chrome.exe"
          replace: "Google Chrome"
        - match: "Code.exe"
          replace: "Visual Studio Code"
```

Use the exact `rewrite` structure as documented in the “rewrite options” section of the same file (not fully shown in the provided snippet).

---

If you paste your current `activ…` widget config from your YAML, I can show the exact minimal changes you need to make.

## Reference Answer
First idea that comes to mind, could use a rewrite rule such as
```yaml
rewrite:
- pattern: "(.+?) - (Google Chrome|Brave|Firefox)$"
  replacement: "\\2"
  ```
  Adjust as needed. I actually use the reverse of that (ie. `\\1` instead of `\\2`) to strip the application name from the title. Alternatively you could just display the process name instead of the title, but that's probably not what you're looking for.
